sentences.text: Gemmiger formicilis is a strictly anaerobic bacterium whose morphology and physiology were studied in isolates from chicken caeca.
Its cells are highly pleomorphic, have a trilaminar cell wall like Gram-negative bacteria, and grow by polar swelling that resembles budding.
The species also lives in the human gut, where studies count it among the butyrate-producing commensals.
In an integrated analysis, higher fruit fibre intake was associated with more Gemmiger formicilis and with butyric-acid-producing enzymes.
In adults, its abundance increased together with other commensals after consumption of water kefir.
